Luchynets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Luchynets's Jewish cemetery, established according to the Commission for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage sometime between the 17th and 18th centuries, remains in use today, with a few hundred headstones dating mostly to the 20th century. The town's Jewish community, numbering 1,050 by 1897, owned nearly every shop in town by 1914; under Romanian administration as part of the Transnistria Governorate, a ghetto here held 2,700 Jews expelled from Bessarabia and Bukovina, and 1,700 of them died alongside hundreds of local Jews.
